channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Why Building a Crosswalk in LA Is Kafkaesque
item.description: Bill McBride did not just predict the 2008 housing bubble, he helped invent financial blogging with his Calculated Risk newsletter. Zach Lasry, meanwhile, is much newer to the scene, but in his career as a real estate developer, he is already responsible for building one of LA's hottest new neighborhoods — Melrose Hill. We spoke to both of them at our live show at the Vermont Hollywood, for a wide-ranging panel discussion on LA real estate. We talk about the difficulty of sourcing construction components, the Kafkaesque process of getting a crosswalk built in LA, and how self-driving cars might help reshape the city and solve its longstanding issues with parking. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sony to Skip CES Show After Honda EV Venture Dropped
item.description: Sony Group Corp. is skipping the CES technology show in 2027, ending a decades-long presence at the Las Vegas electronics showcase in favor of a growing focus on entertainment content.
item.dc:creator: Mayumi Negishi

item.title: Sinha: Private Credit Market Remains Positive for Asia
item.description: Lighthouse Canton Global Asset Management MD & CEO Sanket Sinha believes Asia's private credit is moving beyond the headline artificial intelligence (AI) investment and more into physical and financial infrastructure around AI. He speaks with Haslinda Amin on "Insight with Haslinda Amin." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: TSMC Affiliate Plans Second Singapore Chip Plant in Asia Push
item.description: A venture by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.’s smaller affiliate Vanguard International Semiconductor Corp. is considering a second chipmaking plant in Singapore to meet growing demand.
item.dc:creator: Gao Yuan

item.title: Polish Space Startup Eycore Taps Demand for Sovereign Satellite Intelligence
item.description: Polish space-tech startup Eycore Sp zoo expects its revenue to multiply annually, capitalizing on European governments’ scramble to secure sovereign satellite intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Maciej Martewicz and Konrad Krasuski

item.title: The Stocks That Could Survive an AI Bust
item.description: Merryn Somerset Webb speaks with Blue Whale Growth Fund Chief Investment Officer Stephen Yiu about what could derail the artificial intelligence boom — and where investors might look if it does. They discuss whether today’s enthusiasm is masking an earnings bubble, how investors can diversify beyond AI and which emerging technologies and geopolitical risks could reshape the market next. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Verisure Bets on AI Partnerships to Counter Disruption Concerns
item.description: Verisure Plc is bringing in outside technology and investing more in training artificial intelligence models on its own data as the Swedish home-security business seeks to reassure investors that it can keep up with new competition.
item.dc:creator: Charles Daly

item.title: Belgium’s Agfa to Merge Digital Printing Unit with Siris’ EFI
item.description: Belgium printer IT company Agfa Gevaert NV is merging its digital printer solutions business with Electronics for Imaging Inc., an industrial printer company owned by US private equity firm Siris, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Liana Baker

item.title: China’s Industrial Profits Grow at Weakest Since November Slump
item.description: China’s industrial enterprises saw their earnings grow at the weakest since they fell last November, highlighting the limits of a recovery disproportionately driven by elevated oil costs and sectors linked to artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: China Tech Needs AI Catalyst to Close Valuation Gap, BI Says
item.description: China’s technology stocks will need a domestic artificial intelligence catalyst to close their valuation gap with US technology peers, Bloomberg Intelligence said.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: AI Breaches Add to Safety Fears as Trump Meets Anthropic Chief
item.description: Global anxiety over artificial intelligence risks has intensified following fresh disclosures about a far wider range of breaches by advanced AI models, setting the stage for a high-stakes meeting between Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei and President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Michael Shepard, Maggie Eastland and Courtney Subramanian

item.title: Shein Faces First Public Earnings Test as Growth Woes Mount
item.description: Shein Global Holdings Ltd. reports its first earnings as a public company this week, with investors watching whether it can steady a stock that’s already down nearly 28% since listing amid slowing demand, rising costs and mounting regulatory pressure.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: From Geisha Face Paint to Servers, Sakai Chemical Emerges as AI Linchpin
item.description: Sakai Chemical Industry Co.’s century-old expertise in producing fine powders for face makeup used by geisha is finding a lucrative new use — powering the artificial intelligence boom.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Mochizuki

item.title: Anthropic CEO Amodei to Meet Trump as AI Safety Fears Rise
item.description: Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei is set to have dinner with President Donald Trump on Sunday night, with the meeting bringing together two men at opposite ends of the artificial intelligence safety debate.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland and Courtney Subramanian

item.title: China May Let Alibaba Buy Nvidia RTX Chips, Information Says
item.description: The Chinese government has signaled it may allow companies such as Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. and ByteDance Ltd to buy Nvidia Corp.’s new RTX Pro 5500 chips, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Se Young Lee

item.title: AI Safety Concerns Put Congress on the Spot
item.description: Democratic Rep. Don Beyer of Virginia tells Bloomberg This Weekend that recent AI incidents have increased the urgency for federal safeguards, including safety testing and mandatory reporting of serious problems involving advanced models. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Beyer, co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Artificial Intelligence Caucus, says Congress should create a regulatory structure that combines federal oversight with technical expertise from AI companies. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Humanoid Robots Might Be the Future of Elder Care
item.description: The US spends roughly $400 billion a year on long-term care, and for every 100 people over 65, only four formal caregivers exist. Humanoid robots like Abi, built by Andromeda to provide emotional companionship for dementia patients, are an early attempt to ease that pressure. Andromeda COO Jennifer Haroon, Brookings researcher Gopi Goda, 1X Chief Designer Dar Sleeper, and Nvidia's Kimberly Powell discuss whether robots can truly help solve the elder care crisis, or whether the technology still has too far to go. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta’s VR Glasses Are Exactly What the Apple Vision Pro Should Have Been
item.description: Apple weighs what to do next with its headset.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: Bill Gates Says Trump Is Wrong to Hold Out Against AI Safeguards
item.description: Microsoft Corp. co-founder Bill Gates said government safeguards against potentially catastrophic artificial intelligence risks won’t hamper the US in its competition with China, contrasting with President Donald Trump’s largely hands-off approach.
item.dc:creator: Tony Czuczka

item.title: Australia Senate Requests OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs Face AI Inquiry
item.description: The heads of artificial intelligence firms OpenAI and Anthropic PBC have been called on to appear before an Australian Senate inquiry to answer questions after the recent revelation of a hack of a government website.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger
